subject: Dedicated capacity commitments — KV budget and precision tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara@acura-thera.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acura-thera.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial ask

Thanks Priyom — quick context from our side. We ran a short evaluation of the 32k model family and saw a heavy tail of long-document queries: ~18% of requests need 50k+ context (most are extractive QA across clinical records). Our procurement team asked for a committed pool with predictable latency under 120ms p50 for generation.

Questions: 1) For the 50k KV workload, what does a reserved GPU pool look like assuming we move to INT8 for forward pass? 2) Do you support hot-cache residency vs. streaming KV from host memory for dedicated?

Attaching a simple CSV of our traffic slices. Can you sketch a conservative sizing and call out risks?

— Sara
Clinical ML Lead
Acura Therapeutics
[attachment: acu-traffic-slices.csv (CSV)]

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sara Kim <sara@acura-thera.com>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acura-thera.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial ask

Sara — thanks, this is the right level of detail. High-level takeaways after a quick pass: 1) At 50k effective context with full KV in GPU memory, a single A40-class GPU (48GB) won't fit the working set if you run 2 concurrent streams. For throughput and latency headroom we recommend either: a) INT8 + per-layer KV compression to reduce per-token KV to ~37% of FP16, or b) keep FP16 but move KV to pinned host RAM with NVMe-backed offload for cold prefixes.

I'm attaching a short proposal that sketches three commitment options: "Baseline" (conservative: FP16, host-KV offload, dedicated pool of 8 GPUs), "Optimized" (INT8 + 4 GPUs + aggressive batching limits), and "Hybrid" (mix of INT8 for short flows and FP16 for long-job canaries, 6 GPUs). Each option lists expected p50/p95 and cost delta.

Quick asks from your side: - Confirm target p95 SLO and acceptable cost range. - Which percent of queries must be kept on-GPU KV for acceptable latency?

I also flagged the security/attestation notes for private deploys in the proposal; happy to walk through tomorrow.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: acu-fleet-proposal-v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acura-thera.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Kim <sara@acura-thera.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-03T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial ask

Priyom, thanks — quick internal note: procurement prefers a single SKU to simplify billing, but we can accept a canary strategy for the first release. Our initial SLO target is p50 < 100ms, p95 < 400ms for generation (end-to-end). Budget constraint: ~$45k/month committed.

We can consider INT8 if end-user quality remains within a 3% ROUGE/QA delta. Do you have empirical evals for the 32k model family on INT8?

If you can turn that proposal into a 2-page mutual action plan with target dates (PO, provisioning, pilot, GA) we'll route internally. Carlos

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acura-thera.com>, Sara Kim <sara@acura-thera.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-03T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — mutual action plan draft

Carlos/Sara — looping in Rishi from infra to call out the quant/latency tradeoffs and a conservative provisioning cadence. Rishi, short summary of constraints: Acura needs committed pool under $45k/mo, p95 < 400ms, ~18% of traffic >50k context. They prefer a single SKU with a canary allowance.

Rishi, can you briefly confirm: with mixed INT8/FP16 profile and 6x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs we can meet their p95 if we keep hot KV residency for the top 70% of prefixes and offload cold KV? If not, what does a minimal configuration look like?

I drafted a 2-week pilot plan: Week 0: PO and security paperwork; Week 1: provisioning + model variant upload; Week 2: pilot traffic (swept at 20% of production) + quality checks. If pilot passes, scale to committed pool within 10 business days.

— Lauren
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acura-thera.com>, Sara Kim <sara@acura-thera.com>
Date: 2028-11-04T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — KV budget confirmation and risks

Folks — quick infra readout. Summary: 1) Configuration that balances Acura's budget and SLOs is the Hybrid option: 6x A100-80GB-class slots (or equivalent), with model compiled to allow INT8 inference on short-path flows and FP16 canaries for long-context queries. 2) KV strategy: keep top 70% of prefix tokens resident in GPU VRAM (hot set) using an LRU-prefetch heuristic, stream the remaining KV from pinned host RAM with NVMe read-ahead for cold prefixes. 3) Expected performance: p50 ~ 60–90ms, p95 ~ 280–380ms depending on burstiness and batch coalescing. Risk notes: a) Quantization risk — some QA extractive tasks show a 2–4% drop on INT8; we recommend a quality gate in pilot. b) Tail latency — simultaneous large-context bursts can push p95 above 400ms unless we enable short-term burst capacity (1–2 GPUs warm).

Operational asks to finalize: - Acura to confirm acceptable QA delta threshold for INT8 (we'll run the eval suite). - Sign PO for 6 GPUs + 2 GPU burst buffer for first 3 months. - Agree pilot window and access for our instrumentation team (tracing + token-level cost logs).

I attached a small spreadsheet with simulation outputs for different hot-set sizes and quant profiles. If you're comfortable, we can convert the Hybrid config into the single SKU for billing and include a canary exception clause.

Rishi Malhotra
Infra Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: kv-budget-simulations.xlsx (XLSX)]
